extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and usage rules for writing and editing news copy to Reuters style, covering word choice, capitalization, grammar, names, and journalistic usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: incredible, incredulous
rubrics_metrics.description: Incredible is unbelievable, incredulous is sceptical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index, indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indexes as the plural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indians (U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Native American (capitalised) is preferred, bearing in mind that this includes e.g. Inuit who are not Indians. American Indian is acceptable. Where possible, be more specific and give the name of the tribe (eg. Navajo, Cherokee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See race

rubrics_metrics.name: indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Best avoided because it implies subjective interpretation by the correspondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: indict
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the suggestion that somebody is being judged without trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'indicted on a charge of robbing', not 'indicted for robbing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: indirect speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not retain the present indicative in indirect or reported speech. Change is to was; are to were; will and shall to would; has and have to had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: lead paragraphs with the source at the end where converting would cause lack of clarity. Usually unnecessary to follow 'said' with 'that'. Example: 'Giant Oil Corp will order three supertankers ... next month, the company said.' If source at beginning: 'Giant Oil Corp said it would order...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Indochina
rubrics_metrics.description: No longer used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Now use Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indonesian names
rubrics_metrics.description: Often Indonesians only have one name e.g. Suharto.

rubrics_metrics.name: indoor, indoors
rubrics_metrics.description: Indoor is the adjective, indoors is the adverb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'He stayed indoors to let off the indoor firework.'

rubrics_metrics.name: industrial action
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid this euphemism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you mean a strike, say so. If not a strike, be specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: in fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Can almost always be excised.

rubrics_metrics.name: infant
rubrics_metrics.description: Child up to 12 months old.

rubrics_metrics.name: infer
rubrics_metrics.description: A speaker or writer implies by insinuating or suggesting indirectly. A listener or reader infers by drawing a conclusion from what is said.

rubrics_metrics.name: inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: A persistent rise in the prices of goods and services, caused by too much money chasing too few goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Causes can include increase in money supply, government spending, or contraction in supply. Distinguish demand-pull (excess demand) and cost-push (increased costs of production). The rate of inflation is often a primary policy target for governments and central banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: injuries, wounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Wounds are suffered in combat or are inflicted by weapons or war, injuries by accident or criminal attack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as specific as possible: 'His right leg was broken' not 'His leg was broken.' Use 'suffered' rather than 'sustained' or 'received'. Avoid 'hospitalise' as a verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: innocent
rubrics_metrics.description: Report a plea or a verdict as it was made in court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it was 'not guilty', do not report it as 'innocent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: in order to
rubrics_metrics.description: As a prepositional phrase, just 'to' will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: inpatient
rubrics_metrics.description: One word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not 'enquire', 'enquiry' (see inquire/inquiry note elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: insignia
rubrics_metrics.description: Strictly a plural noun but can be treated as singular as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Each of the guilds had an insignia.'

rubrics_metrics.name: install
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'instal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation but instalment.

rubrics_metrics.name: instil, instilled
rubrics_metrics.description: Instillation but instilment.

rubrics_metrics.name: instinctive, instinctual
rubrics_metrics.description: Instinctive is prompted by instinct, instinctual is belonging to or related to instincts.

rubrics_metrics.name: in spite of
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'despite'.

rubrics_metrics.name: insure
rubrics_metrics.description: Insure means to guarantee against loss, ensure to make sure.

rubrics_metrics.name: international community
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid unless it clearly refers to the body of global diplomatic opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific instead, e.g. 'the United States and its allies' or 'Muslim countries.'

rubrics_metrics.name: International Court of Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the proper title of the World Court in The Hague, the main U.N. judicial body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'World Court' at second reference. The Court settles international disputes submitted by states and gives advisory opinions on legal questions referred by international agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Criminal Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The court set up in The Hague under the auspices of the United Nations to try crimes such as genocide.

rubrics_metrics.name: international date line
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: internecine
rubrics_metrics.description: Internecine means deadly or murderous as well as conflict within a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tautology such as 'internecine warfare.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: A global data communications system comprising hardware and software that connects computers. The World Wide Web consists of content accessed using the Internet and is not synonymous with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalise as a noun, lower case as an adjective (e.g. 'internet banking', 'internet cafe'). The Internet carries email, downloadable software, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpol
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Criminal Police Organisation (Lyon, France).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpol can be used at all references.

rubrics_metrics.name: interval
rubrics_metrics.description: An interval is the time between two events. Do not use it to mean simply elapsed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct: 'There was an interval of a year between his two degrees.' Wrong: 'He studied for an interval of three years.' 'An interval of' can often be excised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intifada
rubrics_metrics.description: Arabic for 'uprising'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe Palestinian uprisings; capitalise.

rubrics_metrics.name: into
rubrics_metrics.description: One word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'on to' as two words where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: intranet
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The name used by the people of northern Canada to describe themselves; singular is Inuk, the language is Inuktitut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 56,000 Inuit live in area from Labrador to Alaska.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariably
rubrics_metrics.description: Means fixed and without exception, not usual or frequent or commonly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Invariably the children catch colds' is wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: inveigh, inveigle
rubrics_metrics.description: Inveigh is to revile or to attack with words. Inveigle is to entice, cajole or wheedle.

rubrics_metrics.name: invoke, evoke
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoke means to call upon solemnly, evoke to bring to mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'In a speech evoking memories of the civil war he invoked God’s help...'

rubrics_metrics.name: IOC
rubrics_metrics.description: International Olympic Committee (Lausanne).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See www.ioc.org

rubrics_metrics.name: IOM
rubrics_metrics.description: International Organization for Migration (Geneva).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.N. intergovernmental agency that moves refugees and migrants to new homes. See www.iom.int

rubrics_metrics.name: IRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Irish Republican Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used alone at first reference from a dateline in the British Isles. If full name is used at first reference the initials need not be bracketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: irascible
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'irrascible.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use 'Eire' for the Republic of Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Northern Ireland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irian Jaya
rubrics_metrics.description: Indonesian province now known as Papua.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It borders Papua New Guinea.

rubrics_metrics.name: ironically
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only rarely and with the greatest care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word has several meanings and most are misunderstood and misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: irregardless
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a double negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'regardless.'

rubrics_metrics.name: -isation, -ization
rubrics_metrics.description: For stories outside the Americas when there is a choice between -isation and –ization for a noun ending use -isation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For stories in the Americas when there is a choice use –ization (American style).

rubrics_metrics.name: -ise, -ize
rubrics_metrics.description: For stories outside the Americas when there is a choice between -ise and -ize for a verb ending use -ise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Americas when there is a choice use –ize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Islam
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion practised by Muslims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Islamic
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to Muslim as an adjective; often used more widely to describe architecture, art, banking, culture, law etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Islamic state is a country ruled by Islamic law (sharia). A Muslim country is one whose population is predominantly Muslim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Islamist
rubrics_metrics.description: A person or organisation advocating a political ideology based on Islam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is not a pejorative term. Only some Islamists advocate violence — describe those as 'militant Islamists.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Islamisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'Islamicisation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain with a phrase depending on context, e.g. 'the imposition of Islamic law (sharia)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Israeli names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'ch' rather than 'h' in transliterating Israeli names into English, e.g. Chaim not Haim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'h' form only if we know it is the individual’s personal preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: it (ships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the pronoun 'it' rather than 'she' when referring to ships.

rubrics_metrics.name: its, it's
rubrics_metrics.description: The possessive pronoun has no apostrophe, unlike the contraction 'it’s' meaning 'it is.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the contraction unless quoting someone. 'Its' as a possessive is often superfluous; rewrite where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacuzzi
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered name of a brand of whirlpool products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'whirlpool bath.'

rubrics_metrics.name: jail, jailer
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'gaol', 'gaoler.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the United States, a jail holds prisoners serving sentences for misdemeanours (<= 1 year) or awaiting trial; prison is for convicted felons serving longer sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Japanese legal system
rubrics_metrics.description: Libel and slander laws in Japan are vague. Police confirmation of criminal investigations is rare; Reuters pickups of Japanese media reports would probably not be actionable in Japan but could be abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspects in Japan can be held 48 hours before formal arrest, then further 72 hours until prosecutor decides; it can take up to 20 more days before indictment is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Jargon is specialised language unfamiliar to the average reader, e.g. remuneration, de-escalation, methodology, going forward, thought leadership, downside risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless directly quoting someone, convert jargon into clear English. Avoid journalism jargon (newsflow, obits, stringers, paras, rejigs). Words like 'obituary' should be written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: jeep, Jeep
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case for a military vehicle. Upper case for the brand of civilian vehicle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jerusalem
rubrics_metrics.description: Israelis and Arabs dispute the status of the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'Jerusalem' as a synonym for Israel (e.g. 'the Jerusalem government'). Be aware of contested status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jesus Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful using 'Christ' because it is a theological term for 'Messiah', a title non-Christians would not give him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Jesus Christ' on first reference in most general stories and 'Jesus' after that. 'Christ' on second reference should be limited to strictly Christian theological contexts. In stories about non-Christian perspectives, use 'Jesus Christ' only if they do.

rubrics_metrics.name: jets
rubrics_metrics.description: Most modern airliners and military aircraft have jet engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use terms like 'jet airliner' or 'jetliner' unless jet-powered is relevant. Specify if propeller driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jew
rubrics_metrics.description: Use for both men and women.

rubrics_metrics.name: jibe / gibe / gybe
rubrics_metrics.description: A gibe is a taunt or sneer, to gybe is to swing a sail over or alter course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In American style a 'gibe' is a taunt or sneer, a 'jibe' is to swing a sail over or to be in accord.

rubrics_metrics.name: jihad
rubrics_metrics.description: An Islamic holy war or struggle; can also refer to an individual's moral struggle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with extreme care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jihadi, jihadist
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use, except in quotes; has become a loaded term.

rubrics_metrics.name: jittery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'anxious' or 'nervous' or 'frightened.'

rubrics_metrics.name: jodhpurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'jodpurs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: John F. Kennedy Space Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Florida, USA. 'Kennedy Space Center' is an acceptable contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mission control is usually at Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in Houston and 'Johnson Space Center' is the acceptable contraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: join together
rubrics_metrics.description: Just 'join' will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalese
rubrics_metrics.description: Trite expressions to avoid (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clichés like 'thumbs up', 'the bottom line', 'ground-breaking', 'magic bullet', 'major' (unless contrasted), 'landmark', 'last-ditch', etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: judgment, not judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'judgment' not 'judgement.'

rubrics_metrics.name: judo, ju-jitsu
rubrics_metrics.description: judo is a modern form of ju-jitsu, Japanese wrestling.

rubrics_metrics.name: jumbo jet
rubrics_metrics.description: Loosely a large, wide-bodied airliner, specifically the Boeing 747.

rubrics_metrics.name: junkie
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use for 'narcotics addict,' unless in quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: junta
rubrics_metrics.description: A political clique or a government formed by such a clique, usually after a revolution or coup.

rubrics_metrics.name: jury
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'The jury has reached its decision.'

rubrics_metrics.name: just deserts
rubrics_metrics.description: What you deserve, not 'desserts' which you have for pudding.

rubrics_metrics.name: justify
rubrics_metrics.description: To defend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use: 'The prime minister tried to justify the decision', not 'The prime minister justified the decision.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Kaaba
rubrics_metrics.description: Islam’s most sacred shrine at the centre of the great mosque in Mecca.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe dimensions if relevant; e.g. a mass of stone 38 feet high, 40 long and 30 wide (11 x 12 x 9 metres).

rubrics_metrics.name: karat / carat
rubrics_metrics.description: A measurement of weight in precious stones and of purity in gold in American style: 'karat' in US; 'carat' in UK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kathmandu
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Kathmandu', not 'Katmandu', Nepal.

rubrics_metrics.name: kerosene
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'kerosine'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medium-light distillate used for lighting and heating and to fuel jet and turbo-prop engines. Called 'paraffin' or 'paraffin oil' in Britain.

rubrics_metrics.name: ketchup
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'catchup' or 'catsup.'

rubrics_metrics.name: key
rubrics_metrics.description: Overused as an adjective and usually superfluous.

rubrics_metrics.name: keynote
rubrics_metrics.description: One word as in 'keynote speech' or 'keynote address'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative phrasing because it's a tired cliché—explain why the speech is keynote.

rubrics_metrics.name: KGB
rubrics_metrics.description: Initials of the former Soviet Committee for State Security (Komitet Gosudarstvennoi Bezopasnosti), split up and renamed in 1991.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successor Russian agencies may be referred to as successors to the KGB, but do not include the Interior Ministry in charge of the police.

rubrics_metrics.name: Khmer Rouge
rubrics_metrics.description: Cambodian Communists.

rubrics_metrics.name: kibbutz
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural 'kibbutzim.' An Israeli collective settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: kickoff, kick off
rubrics_metrics.description: One word for the noun and two words for the verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: kidnap, kidnapping, kidnapped, kidnapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Use these forms as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: kids
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'children.'

rubrics_metrics.name: kilogram
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'kg' (no full stop, same singular and plural) at all references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert kilograms to pounds for small weights (below 1,000 kg), to tons for larger weights. Conversion approximations and precise multipliers provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: kilometre
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'km' (no full stop, same singular and plural) at all references, except in phrases like 'hundreds of kilometres.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert to miles (rough approx and precise multipliers provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: km per hour / kph
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'km per hour' on first reference, 'kph' on second and subsequent references.

rubrics_metrics.name: kiloton
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of explosive force, equal to that of 1,000 tons of TNT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Hiroshima bomb was 12.5 kiloton.

rubrics_metrics.name: kindergarten
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'kindergarten.'

rubrics_metrics.name: king
rubrics_metrics.description: At second reference either 'the king' or the full name, e.g. King Baudouin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize titles of deposed monarchs, e.g. 'ex-King Zahir Shah.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Kolkata
rubrics_metrics.description: Not 'Calcutta', India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean names
rubrics_metrics.description: Koreans put their surname first. The given name follows, hyphenated, with first part initial upper case and second part initial lower case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Kim Dae-jung, Roh Moo-hyun, Ahn Jung-hwan. Use surname only at second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: kph
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'km per hour' on first reference, 'kph' on subsequent references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ku Klux Klan
rubrics_metrics.description: A loose-knit organisation of about 40 U.S. groups claiming white supremacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: kudos
rubrics_metrics.description: Fame, credit or renown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: laager, lager
rubrics_metrics.description: A laager is a defensive encampment; lager is a type of beer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labour Party, Labor Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the convention used for proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note Australian 'Labor Party' spelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: lady
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'woman.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible in team title such as 'Fulham Ladies’ football club.' Where organisers use 'Ladies’ Championship', substitute 'women’s championship.'

rubrics_metrics.name: lame duck, lame-duck
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the noun, hyphenated for the adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land Rover
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade mark. Capitalised. No hyphen.

rubrics_metrics.name: large-scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid if 'big' is shorter and usually better.

rubrics_metrics.name: last/past/latest
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Last' refers to times up to the present. 'Past' is vaguer. Use 'latest' if 'last' might confuse most recent with final occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'His latest attempt may not be his last.'

rubrics_metrics.name: late
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use to mean 'dead.'

rubrics_metrics.name: latter, former
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid these expressions because they make readers read backwards to discern meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: laudable, laudatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Laudable is praiseworthy. Laudatory is giving or expressing praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: lay, lie
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay in present tense takes an object; lie does not take a direct object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct conjugations and examples: 'I lay down my arms'; 'I lie down to sleep'; past forms and perfect forms explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: lead, leading, led
rubrics_metrics.description: The past participle is 'led.'

rubrics_metrics.name: leave
rubrics_metrics.description: As a verb, 'leave' is weak and imprecise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a more accurate and active verb. Examples given to prefer more precise wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: liquidity
rubrics_metrics.description: The ease with which financial instruments can be traded and turned into cash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe liquid markets/instruments and opposed concept of illiquid; can also describe cash flow in a business.

rubrics_metrics.name: lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists should be in alphabetical order unless another order is emphasised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: G7 should be written 'comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy Japan and the United States.'

rubrics_metrics.name: literally
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only in quotation since it almost always, in fact, means metaphorically.

rubrics_metrics.name: litre / liter
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'litre' (British); American style is 'liter'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide conversion guidance to gallons with approximations and precise multipliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: loaded words
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'admitted', 'agreed', 'revealed', 'refuted', 'claimed' etc. instead of 'said.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They contain an element of judgment by the reporter; use 'said' where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: loans (reporting guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the verb 'to give' when referring to loans; they are paid for through interest. Do not say someone is 'raising a loan' when it is being arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact name of borrower, guarantees, amount, maturity, interest rate. Report fees paid to banks. Define refinancing, restructuring, rescheduling, moratorium, repudiation, default — and advise clarity about nature of any default declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: long term, long-term
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the noun, one word hyphenated for the adjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'They had a long-term relationship which endured for the long term.'

rubrics_metrics.name: long time, longtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the noun, one word for the adjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Theirs was a longtime friendship which lasted a long time.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lord’s
rubrics_metrics.description: The London cricket ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note apostrophe.

rubrics_metrics.name: lorry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'truck.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Luxembourg
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Luxembourg.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lycra
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generic terms such as 'stretch fabric.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Maastricht Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the proper name where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mach number
rubrics_metrics.description: Mach 1, Mach 2 etc. The Mach number is the ratio of an aircraft’s speed through the air compared with the speed of sound in the same conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: macroeconomic
rubrics_metrics.description: No hyphen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madagascar
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Malagasy' for the people and the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: man, mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'humanity' when referring to the human race.

rubrics_metrics.name: manifesto, manifestos
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'manifesto' (singular) and 'manifestos' (plural).

rubrics_metrics.name: marines
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize when referring to the U.S. Marine Corps or its members (e.g. 'Six U.S. Marines').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not refer to them as 'soldiers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: masterful/masterly
rubrics_metrics.description: Masterly means very skilful and worthy of a master. Masterful is imperious and domineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example distinctions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: materialise / materialize
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you mean take bodily form it is simpler to write 'happen' or 'occur' or 'take place.'

rubrics_metrics.name: may, can / may, might
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on modal verbs is signposted at the end of the chunk.
